claims.text: The European Union scheduled emergency talks for Tuesday to discuss the migration crisis in Ceuta following tense exchanges between Spain and other member states.
At least 67 people died during the attempt to cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on July 30.
Twenty-two European Union member states issued a joint letter calling for coordinated action to strengthen the EU's external borders.
Italy suspended its border-free Schengen arrangement with Spain following the Ceuta migration crisis.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez stated that the Spanish government fully restored control over the border and prevented unauthorized onward movement in less than 48 hours.
Spanish police began installing a 500-metre floating barrier off the border with Morocco to prevent illegal migration by water.
President of Ceuta Juan Jesús Vivas stated that several thousand people still need to be returned to Morocco and an atmosphere of unease remains.
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani blamed the situation in Ceuta on the Spanish government's prior scheme to regularise undocumented migrants.
U.S. President Donald Trump described the crossing of migrants into Ceuta as a 'catastrophe' and an 'invasion'.
Ceuta and Melilla form the European Union's only land borders with the African continent.
An estimated 50,000 to 60,000 undocumented migrants crossed into Ceuta from Morocco during the border crisis.
Spain's Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares stated on social media that virtually all those who entered Ceuta had returned to Morocco.
To reach Ceuta by water, migrants often swim approximately five kilometres from the Moroccan town of Fnideq.
U.S. embassies across ten Middle Eastern countries issued security alerts advising American citizens to consider leaving the region or prepare for departure at short notice.
Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's military central command, warned that any country serving as a defensive shield for the U.S. will be engulfed by the flames of war.
An unknown projectile struck a tanker off the coast of Oman on Saturday amid heightened regional tensions.
A drone struck a U.S.-owned gas vessel moored in an Egyptian port on Wednesday, causing a fire.
Iran and the United States have been engaged in direct military conflict since February 28.
U.S. European Command chief General Alexus Grynkewich warned Pentagon officials that the U.S. lacks sufficient naval assets to continue intercepting Iranian ballistic missile attacks on Israel.

An assessment by the Center for Strategic and International Studies indicated that the U.S. military consumed over 20 percent of its Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles during the conflict with Iran.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel desires to strike Iran's energy targets, but the U.S. has not approved it due to concerns over a global oil crisis.
Kuwait's army reported that its air defences destroyed multiple Iranian drones within Kuwaiti airspace.
Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar urged Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to avoid attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers.
The Indian Ministry of External Affairs reported to Parliament that 16 Indian citizens, including 10 seafarers, have been killed during the Middle East conflict.
Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja died in an avalanche while leading an expedition on Broad Peak in Pakistan.
Ten climbers were killed in the avalanche that struck Broad Peak in Pakistan's Karakoram mountain range.
Pakistani officials recovered the bodies of American climber Mallory Geis, Omani climber Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, and Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung.
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah confirmed the deaths of six Nepalese and four foreign climbers in the Broad Peak avalanche.
Nirmal Purja rose to global fame in 2019 by climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre peaks in six months and six days.
Broad Peak, standing at 8,047 metres, is the world's 12th-highest summit.
Elite Exped, co-founded by Nirmal Purja, confirmed the deaths of Purja and his climbing partners Pur Bahadur Gurung and Nima Sherpa.
Nirmal Purja served in the British military for 16 years, including time in the Brigade of Gurkhas and the Special Boat Squadron.
In January 2021, Nirmal Purja led the first team to complete a winter ascent of K2, the world's second-highest mountain.
A Russian overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv killed nine people and injured more than 30 others.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia launched 35 missiles and 185 attack drones in the barrage against Kyiv.
Ukrainian air defenses intercepted only one of 27 Russian ballistic missiles due to a critical shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles.
Ukrainian drones struck three oil refineries in Russia's Bashkortostan region, roughly 1,000 miles from the front lines.
A sanctioned Russian container ship was sunk in the Black Sea following a Ukrainian drone attack.
U.S. President Donald Trump stated he had not made a final decision on granting Ukraine a license to manufacture Patriot interceptor missiles.
Russia's state-owned nuclear operator Rosatom confirmed that all 17 crew members of the container ship Yanina were rescued after the vessel was sunk in the Black Sea.
Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev characterized the Ukrainian drone attack on the container ship Yanina as an act of piracy and robbery.
A Russian missile exploded near the Lithuanian embassy in Kyiv, causing structural damage to the building but no injuries.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino scrapped plans to sell minority stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private equity investors following intense backlash.
European soccer governing body UEFA and CONCACAF publicly criticized Gianni Infantino's leadership following the abandoned investment proposal.
UEFA stated that the current FIFA leadership has lost the confidence of UEFA and many other members of the global football community.
Qatar's Football Association publicly backed Gianni Infantino's leadership while welcoming the decision to drop the stake sale plan.
The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) declared that it no longer has confidence in Gianni Infantino's leadership following the flawed proposal process.
Carlos Cordeiro, special adviser to Gianni Infantino, resigned from his position in protest against the World Cup stake sale proposal.
FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour stated that FIFA's own administration was deceived regarding the private investment project.
The proposed plan sought to create a commercial entity to manage FIFA competitions and sell a 20 percent stake to private investors.
FIFA selected Thrive Capital, founded by Joshua Kushner, to lead the private investor group for the proposed World Cup commercial entity.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi to apologize for police violence during the July 20 student march in Delhi.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a video message stating he forgives youth protesters who used abusive language against him and his late mother, calling them 'misguided children'.
Indian authorities registered a Zero FIR over a viral video showing a young protester using abusive language against Prime Minister Modi.
The student protest movement erupted across India in July following national exam paper leaks that forced a retest for two million students.
The youth political group Cockroach Janta Party accumulated over 26 million followers on Instagram since its launch in May.
Protester Shradha Singh faced severe online harassment, including death and rape threats, after uploading a satirical Instagram reel during the Delhi protests.
Social media network Meta removed 33 posts documenting the youth protests from Shradha Singh's Instagram account.
Incessant heavy rainfall and landslides in Kerala resulted in six confirmed deaths across the state.
Authorities in Kerala established 65 relief camps, providing shelter to 1,465 displaced residents.
The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert for eight Kerala districts, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall.
Floodwaters inundated a poultry farm in Pala, Kottayam district, killing approximately 2,500 chickens.
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan reported that 17 houses were completely destroyed and 127 suffered partial damage during the severe weather.
Landslides in Idukki district killed 65-year-old Sumathi in Adoormala and 77-year-old Prabhakaran Nair in Vagamon.
The Kozhikode District Disaster Management Authority restricted heavy vehicle traffic on the Thamarassery ghat road due to safety concerns from rain and landslips.
Search operations were launched in Kannur district for two missing individuals swept away by swollen rivers.
Terrorists shot dead two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh in the Kellam area of south Kashmir's Kulgam district on Friday evening.
Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai announced an ex-gratia financial assistance of 20 lakh rupees for the families of each killed worker.
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah announced 10 lakh rupees in ex-gratia relief and an additional 6 lakh rupees from the district administration for the families of the victims.
The victims were identified as 24-year-old Deepak Ratray and 28-year-old Bopinder Kumar, both brick kiln workers from Chhattisgarh.
Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha ordered security agencies to conduct a comprehensive review of Standard Operating Procedures established to protect non-local labourers.
The attack in Kulgam was the second targeted killing of security personnel or workers in Jammu and Kashmir within two weeks, following the July 22 killing of Head Constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi.
